scope: Read-only review of the real R02 analytic rebuild and material compilation paths. Only this report is written; no kernel, precision, threshold, rounding, source asset or golden changed; no additional physics solve run.

inheritedEvidence.summary: source_audit found exact module/minified-worker analytic, spec, binding, initial positions and measurements equality within one Node runtime. Chromium paper and material SHA differ while operation, recipe and person match. Its isolated naive/scaled Math.hypot probes did not reproduce Chromium. These results are reused as evidence, not rerun or reinterpreted as an established hypot cause.

actualCallChain: adapter compileWithinNativeBudget -> compileAnalytic -> curveTable / curvePoint -> cdt2d
hashContract materialHash and workerExtension paper SHA

findings.source: editKernel samplePatternEdge, lines 14-23; editBridge sampled, lines 10-17 and rebuildEditedAnalytic lines 47-61
findings.observed: Circle points call Math.cos and Math.sin, including t=0 and t=1. Every edge of every panel is rebuilt, including the protected waistbands. Adaptive quarter/midpoint sampling branches on deviation >0.1 mm and chord distance >8 mm. Signed area and complete paper diagnostics derive from these samples.
findings.inference: Different last bits from an implementation-approximated trig function can change sampledPointsMm and area, hence complete paperSHA256, even when the edit operation and source circle parameters are identical. A branch-count difference is only possible near a threshold and is not demonstrated.

findings.source: editBridge distance, bezierDerivative and curveLength, lines 5 and 19-30; gathering rebuild lines 65-66
findings.observed: Line lengths use Math.hypot. Quadratic/cubic speeds use Math.hypot inside adaptive Simpson integration with eps=1e-7, depth=20 and a 15*eps split criterion. Circle length uses radius*abs(sweepDegrees)*Math.PI/180, without sin/cos. All 20 S03 gathering rows recompute projectedLengthAMm/BMm from these lengths.
findings.inference: Length last-bit differences can enter full paper fields and geometryHash through gathering. This is a candidate, not a diagnosis; source_audit hypot substitutions did not reproduce Chromium.

findings.source: adapter curvePoint and curveTable, lines 3140-3180; compileAnalytic lines 3205-3248
findings.observed: Mesher circlePoint calls sin/cos for interior samples but pins t=0/1 to the exact source vertices. Dense curve tables use ceil(length/0.4), cumulative hypot distances, binary searches on accumulated lengths and arc-length interpolation. Boundary count uses ceil(total/16), doubles when chord error exceeds 0.25 mm, and pairs seam counts. Interior points use a regular sqrt(3) grid, strict inside tests and boundary clearance >0.42*step.
findings.inference: Tiny curve/length differences can directly change boundary UV values before any physics. Near branch boundaries they can also change sample/interior-point counts. Existing counts alone cannot establish equality. No such branch crossing has been demonstrated; sqrt(3) is a fixed grid constant and is not specifically implicated.

findings.kind: observed code plus unconfirmed downstream amplification
findings.source: adapter embedded cdt2d monotone compareEvent lines 787-798 and 885-915; delaunayRefine/testFlip lines 1231-1304; compileAnalytic lines 3250-3253
findings.observed: CDT sorts events using coordinate differences, orientation and index tie breaks. It uses robust-orientation and robust-in-sphere predicates; nonconstrained diagonals flip on inCircle<0 and remain on inCircle>=0. Final triangle winding is corrected by a signed area comparison.
findings.inference: Different input UV values near a co-circular or collinear configuration can choose a different event order/diagonal, even with robust predicates. The predicates are evaluating their actual inputs; this is not evidence of random or faulty triangulation. Compare exact UV, ordered triangles and unordered triangle sets separately. No topology difference has yet been confirmed.

findings.source: operation changeSkirtDesign; sourceRepair prepareNativeSource lines 11-47; adapter gradePaper3 lines 2202-2238 and physical strain/kernel code lines 2616/2784
findings.observed: The requested source vertex edits are arithmetic deltas with cloned placements and curves. No random/time input was found in this pre-solve geometry chain. Math.acos belongs to a legacy short-sleeve grading function not used for this S03 operation; atan2 occurs in later physics/projection code, not in the pre-solve paper rebuild. S03 is PencilSkirt, not SkirtLevels, and its edited local coordinate extent is below the 2000 mm rebase trigger.
findings.implication: Do not attribute the observed pre-solve paper SHA mismatch to inverse trigonometry in unrelated legacy/physics code, solver iteration variability or the inactive source-repair branches.

recipeHash.input: bodyCm, design, baseRecipeHash, operations and editHistory; excludes rebuilt curve samples and material mesh.
recipeHash.implication: Matching recipe/operation is compatible with different derived floating-point samples.

geometryHash.input: Panel ids, verticesMm, edge endpoints/kinds/controlPointsMm/arc, placement and seam ids/references/gathering. It excludes sampledPointsMm, signedAreaMm2 and triangulation.
geometryHash.implication: If this hash also differs, compare its actual fields first, especially recomputed gathering projected lengths. CDT cannot directly cause this upstream hash difference.

paperSHA256.input: JSON.stringify(nextAnalytic), including derived samples, lengths, area, diagnostics and metadata.
paperSHA256.implication: A different SHA does not by itself identify geometry magnitude, topology, key-order or the first differing field. Compare parsed data and exact serialized order, without rounding.

materialSHA256.input: Stable-key JSON of optional elasticStays, panel ids/uvMm/ordered triangles, and seam ids/references/stitchVertexPairs.
materialSHA256.implication: One UV last-bit difference suffices; reordered but geometrically equivalent triangle rows also change the digest. Material hash excludes most analytic diagnostic metadata, so a metadata-only paper difference cannot alone explain material hash drift.

standardsContext.summary: ECMAScript specifies general finite cosine, sine and hypot results as implementation-approximated. Identical JS source therefore does not by itself prove cross-runtime bit identity for these results. This establishes plausibility, not which function caused the present failure.

nextReadOnlyComparison: Use the real complete Chromium paper packet and the same-request Node packet already being collected; do not infer from hashes alone.
Compare operation, authoritative endpoints/control points/arc/placement and gathering first; then edge length/sample counts and the first differing sampled point.
Compare full geometryHash inputs separately from the complete paper serialization.
Compare per-panel UV counts and exact first differing UV, boundary ids and stitch pairs; only then exact and unordered triangle sets.
Retain original failing golden and gates while locating the first divergence. No numerical normalization, rounding, threshold relaxation or blanket runtime exemption is justified by this review.
conclusion: There are real, reachable trig and hypot paths before paper/material hashing, plus downstream discretization and CDT sign branches that can amplify changed inputs. The exact cause and magnitude remain unconfirmed until the real browser packet comparison; this source review does not establish geometric equivalence or authorize publication.
